title: Floyd-Warshall
tagline: All-pairs shortest paths in three tidy loops — O(V³) dynamic programming.

intuition.analogy: Planning road trips between every pair of cities, you ask: 'does routing through city k ever beat my current best?' You consider each possible intermediate city one at a time, and your distance table only improves.
paragraphs: Floyd-Warshall computes shortest distances between every pair of nodes. Its elegance is in the DP formulation: allow intermediate vertices 1..k and ask whether going through vertex k shortens any path.
The recurrence dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j]), looped with k on the outside, fills the whole table in O(V³). It handles negative edges (but not negative cycles).

It's the go-to when V is small (≤ ~400) and you need all pairs — far simpler to code than running Dijkstra V times, and it also computes transitive closure and detects negative cycles (negative on the diagonal).
intuition.keyIdea: For each intermediate k, relax every pair (i, j) through k. k must be the outermost loop.

steps.title: Initialise the matrix
steps.detail: dist[i][j] = edge weight, 0 on the diagonal, ∞ where no edge exists.

steps.title: Triple loop with k outermost
steps.detail: for k, for i, for j: dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j]).

steps.title: Read results
steps.detail: After all k, dist[i][j] is the shortest path. A negative value on dist[i][i] flags a negative cycle.

complexity.timeReason: Three nested loops over all vertices.

pitfalls: k MUST be the outer loop — swapping loop order gives wrong answers.
Guard against overflow (∞ + ∞) by using a sentinel and skipping unreachable pairs.
Impractical for large V because of the cubic time and quadratic memory.

dryRun.clickMoment: Considering C as an intermediate instantly fixes A→B from 4 to 2. Each k pass lets every pair benefit from one more allowed waypoint.

problems.title: Find the City
problems.statement: City with fewest reachable neighbours within a threshold.
problems.hint: Floyd-Warshall, then count reachable nodes per city.

approach: All-pairs shortest paths via Floyd-Warshall, then for each city count how many others are within the distance threshold.
Return the city with the smallest reachable count, breaking ties by the largest index.

problems.title: Course Schedule IV
problems.hint: Transitive closure via Floyd-Warshall on booleans.

approach: The queries ask about reachability (transitive closure). Floyd-Warshall generalises: reach[i][j] = reach[i][j] or (reach[i][k] and reach[k][j]).
Build the closure in O(n^3), then answer each prerequisite query in O(1).

problems.title: Evaluate Division
problems.statement: Answer a/b queries from given ratios.
problems.hint: All-pairs products via a Floyd-Warshall-like propagation.

approach: Treat variables as nodes and a/b = value as a directed edge with that ratio (and 1/value back). Path products give other ratios.
Floyd-Warshall over multiplication: d[i][j] = d[i][k]·d[k][j]. Then each query is a table lookup, or -1 if disconnected.
